arguments.summary: Over the next 63 sessions, NVDA has the stronger reported operating acceleration and relative 63-session market behavior versus QQQ, while MU has the larger conditional valuation dispersion and substantially higher realized volatility. QQQ is a diversified but still meaningful look-through exposure: its dated equity weights were NVDA 8.54% and MU 5.01%, and its sponsor aggregate P/E was 30.08x on an earlier date. This is research sensitivity, not a forecast or allocation.

claims.text: NVDA reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $96.2bn, up 106% year over year, data-center revenue of $89.0bn, up 117%, and GAAP diluted EPS of $2.46. Its reported first-half FY2027 diluted EPS was $4.85 versus FY2026 annual diluted EPS of $4.90; the interim figure is not annualized.

NVDA FY2027 GAAP split-adjusted sensitivity uses assumed EPS/multiples of $7.50/25x, $9.00/30x and $10.50/35x, producing bear/base/bull scenario prices of $187.50, $270.00 and $367.50 relative to the September 18 split-adjusted close. Inputs are assumptions held beyond the 63-session horizon, not consensus, observed P/E, or a forecast.

NVDA's completed 63-session price return was 5.50%, versus QQQ's -2.59%; calculated relative performance was +8.08 percentage points. Its 63-session realized volatility was 39.63%, above QQQ's 20.85%. These are descriptive returns, not causal or predictive.

MU reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $41.46bn, GAAP net income of $28.24bn and GAAP diluted EPS of $24.67. Reported 273-day FY2026 interim diluted EPS was $41.40, compared with FY2025 annual diluted EPS of $7.59; interim EPS is not annualized.

MU FY2026 GAAP split-adjusted sensitivity uses assumed EPS/multiples of $35/18x, $45/22x and $55/26x, producing bear/base/bull scenario prices of $630, $990 and $1,430 relative to the September 18 split-adjusted close. Inputs are assumptions held beyond the 63-session horizon, not consensus, observed P/E, or a forecast.

MU's completed 63-session price return was -10.42%, versus QQQ's -2.59%; calculated relative performance was -7.83 percentage points. MU's 63-session realized volatility was 89.56%, versus QQQ's 20.85%.

QQQ's dated September 18 equity holdings assigned 8.54% to NVDA and 5.01% to MU, with 99.86% reported equity-weight coverage; these are dated fund weights, not current holdings or a portfolio exposure. Sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08x as of August 31 and is not comparable to a company EPS valuation model.

NVDA disclosed that export controls have harmed its competitive position and that it was effectively foreclosed from the China market; it also described dependence on overseas partners, especially Taiwan and South Korea. MU disclosed possible tariff/trade-restriction risk and uncertainty around investigations. The supplied rule changed review of specified advanced semiconductors to case-by-case subject to conditions, but does not quantify issuer impact or establish later policy status.

gaps.description: No verified current policy status after the January 2026 rule and no quantified issuer-specific revenue, profit, or supply impact. This blocks quantified policy-impact conclusions, but not the sourced operational or scenario claims.
No forward consensus or observed issuer P/E is supplied. Scenario EPS and multiples are explicit assumptions, so valuation is conditional rather than an estimate of fair value.

assumptions: Scenario grids use US-GAAP annual EPS and split-adjusted share-basis assumptions; reported interim EPS is an anchor, not annualized.
NVDA's base case requires continued data-center demand conversion and margin resilience; MU's base case requires retention of much of interim earnings strength after Q3.
QQQ comparison uses its dated sponsor holdings and aggregate fund P/E, not synthetic corporate EPS or inferred current composition.
arguments.counter_thesis: NVDA's acceleration may fail to persist amid customer concentration, export controls, and overseas-supply dependence; MU's record results may moderate sharply with memory-cycle, customer, tariff, and execution risks. QQQ's diversification can be preferable if either single-name scenario fails, though it retains dated exposure to both companies.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA's next reported results for data-center revenue, GAAP EPS, customer concentration, and any material export-control/supply disclosure; a material slowdown or restriction would challenge the base assumptions.
Review MU's September 30 fiscal Q4 results for whether earnings, strategic-customer agreements, cash generation and capex support or contradict the assumed FY2026 sensitivity range.
Refresh QQQ sponsor holdings and aggregate valuation before relying on look-through comparisons, because weights and fund characteristics are dated and rebalancing occurs periodically.

shared_exposures.mechanism: AI and data-center demand is a common candidate driver: NVDA reported data-center acceleration; MU describes memory for AI/compute-intensive applications; QQQ held both at dated weights.
shared_exposures.qualification: Exposure is not quantified beyond the dated QQQ weights and does not establish causality or a portfolio allocation.
